budget.domain_randomization: motor-v1: wheel resistance, motor no-load speed, motor torque capacity
budget.selection_rule: Predesignated final checkpoint; no evaluation-based checkpoint selection; no retraining after results.
budget.evaluation_domain: nominal, deterministic, starts at reference frame zero including its nonzero initial velocities
not_claimed: single policy for all six skills

tasks.raw_skill_intent: Forward displacement with flight and stable landing
caveats: Uniform morphology scaling and +5.8 mm global vertical clearance; no retiming.
Starts from reference frame zero with its recorded nonzero velocity; no standstill-to-jump transition tested.

source.description: hop turn 90 degrees left in air

tasks.raw_skill_intent: Original source: 90-degree turn in air; suite gate only tests whole-episode yaw progress plus a separate flight event
caveats: A suite pass DOES NOT establish a 90-degree airborne turn; much of the observed turn happens on the ground.
Root-rotating landmark offsets, uniform morphology scaling and +8.1 mm global vertical clearance; no retiming.
Starts from reference frame zero including its nonzero velocity.

tasks.raw_skill_intent: Lateral jump excursion and return, with stable landing
caveats: Reference has 48.25 mm maximum robot-ground penetration and 120 Hz peak leg speed 25.21 rad/s; these are quality warnings, not a proof of dynamic impossibility.
Only +1 mm initial clearance; no per-frame grounding, global 5 cm lift or retiming to conceal the reference defects.
Net lateral displacement is almost zero; gate also requires substantial lateral excursion.

tasks.raw_skill_intent: Human-inspired rolling-to-stop task, NOT raw human running imitation
caveats: Starts already rolling (reference initial forward velocity about 0.311 m/s); acceleration from standstill is not tested.
Duration doubled, travel scaled by 0.35, vertical change scaled by 0.15, pitch by 0.35; alternating footsteps replaced with symmetric wheel support.
Reference wheel spin is kinematically reconstructed but masked as a training target; policy wheel torque remains learned.

tasks.raw_skill_intent: Human-inspired 18 cm stationary crouch and recovery, NOT unmodified skateboard duck-under
caveats: Source frames 160-330, duration doubled, observed human lowering normalized to an explicit robot depth of 18 cm.
Horizontal travel, roll and yaw removed; small fore-aft wheel rolling maintains static COM support during retargeting.
No overhead obstacle or collision-clearance test was included.

source.description: large step to a short ledge

tasks.raw_skill_intent: Climb a real static ledge and finish with both wheels supported on its top
caveats: Ledge height estimated from terminal foot support, not pelvis; leading edge and depth are estimated, not recorded CMU scene ground truth.
Identical metric static box specification is used by Isaac training/evaluation and MuJoCo deployment; live collider readback required.
Only one ledge geometry and one nominal frame-zero rollout per engine were tested.

limitations: Each task is a separate policy fine-tuned from the same previous jump DR checkpoint.
A completed training process or surviving until motion_end is not task success.
Behavior gates are fixed before outcomes; additional runtime scene audits only strengthen provenance.
Isaac wheel forces are net-force proxies and non-wheel ground-only force evidence is incomplete.
Videos reconstruct recorded physical rollout poses in a common renderer; they are not additional physical simulations.
Raw CMU assets, robot assets, full trajectories, logs and checkpoints are excluded from Git.
